title: Switches - MS software versions MS 18.1.9 changelog

announcements.post_subject: A new Generally Available MS Switch firmware is now available

Important alerts: As part of Cisco's ongoing commitment to proactive security and product quality, the MS engineering team has conducted a comprehensive internal security review. This review resulted in one or more software hardening release(s) that address(e)s multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities.

MS-45667: MS130-24(P) switches will reboot twice during the upgrade process when transitioning to MS 18.1.8 (or later) from MS 18.1.7 or earlier. This behavior is expected, and is not indicative of a problem.
New feature highlights: MS-21883: Group Policy ACL on MS130 & MS150
MS-21889: Maximum MAC support in MAC Allowlists
MS-21885: 802.1x limited access mode with pre-auth GPACL
MS-28340: Local Status Page connectivity diagnostics enhancements
MS-24285: Traffic Mirroring: RSPAN & VLAN Based SPAN
General fixed issues: MS-48884: Resolved an issue that sometimes caused MS150 switches in stacks with configured STP priority values to incorrectly adopt the default STP priority during active switch changeovers
MS-41954: Improved remediation of an issue that caused some MS130 and MS150 switches in stacked configurations to unexpectedly reboot
Ms150 fixed issues: MS-44491: Fixed a bug that sometimes caused mgig switch ports to fail to initialize after being re-enabled by a configured port schedule
Ms225 and ms250 fixed issues: MS-43826: Resolved an issue that caused some switches in stacked configurations to incorrectly drop IGMP join packets, which resulted in delays for clients attempting connect with multicast applications
MS-38887: Fixed a bug that sometimes caused switches in stacked configurations to incorrectly retake the active stack role from another active stack member after being rebooted
General known issues: MS-36608: MS130 and MS150 switches may not properly display IPv6 RA packets in dashboard packet captures
Ms120 known issues: MS-2938: Switches may fail to provide PoE power to legacy access points (always present)
MS-2728: Cable tests may report incorrect cable lengths
Ms130 known issues: MS-38070: MS130X mGig ports may fail to establish a link when both sides are forced to 100 Mbps full-duplex. If either side of the connection uses auto-negotiation the link will be established normally
Ms150 known issues: MS-38370: MS150 switches may intermittently negotiate USB-C Ethernet adapters at 10 Mbps half-duplex instead of the expected speed for the switchport, requiring a physical reseat to correct the issue.
Ms350x known issues: HWMS-375: Switches may experience an unexpected reboot (present since MS 15)
Ms355 known issues: HWMS-378: Switches in stacked configurations may experience some ports failing to reconnect after a firmware upgrade.

Switches - MS software versions MS 18.1.9 changelog

Important alerts

  • As part of Cisco's ongoing commitment to proactive security and product quality, the MS engineering team has conducted a comprehensive internal security review. This review resulted in one or more software hardening release(s) that address(e)s multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities.

  • MS-45667: MS130-24(P) switches will reboot twice during the upgrade process when transitioning to MS 18.1.8 (or later) from MS 18.1.7 or earlier. This behavior is expected, and is not indicative of a problem.

New feature highlights

  • MS-21883: Group Policy ACL on MS130 & MS150

  • MS-21889: Maximum MAC support in MAC Allowlists

  • MS-21885: 802.1x limited access mode with pre-auth GPACL

  • MS-28340: Local Status Page connectivity diagnostics enhancements

  • MS-23684: Layer 2 multicast live tool

  • MS-24285: Traffic Mirroring: RSPAN & VLAN Based SPAN

Fixed issues

  •  

General fixed issues

  • MS-48884: Resolved an issue that sometimes caused MS150 switches in stacks with configured STP priority values to incorrectly adopt the default STP priority during active switch changeovers

  • MS-41954: Improved remediation of an issue that caused some MS130 and MS150 switches in stacked configurations to unexpectedly reboot

Ms150 fixed issues

  • MS-44491: Fixed a bug that sometimes caused mgig switch ports to fail to initialize after being re-enabled by a configured port schedule

Ms225 and ms250 fixed issues

  • MS-43826: Resolved an issue that caused some switches in stacked configurations to incorrectly drop IGMP join packets, which resulted in delays for clients attempting connect with multicast applications

  • MS-38887: Fixed a bug that sometimes caused switches in stacked configurations to incorrectly retake the active stack role from another active stack member after being rebooted

Known issues

  •  

General known issues

  • MS-36608: MS130 and MS150 switches may not properly display IPv6 RA packets in dashboard packet captures

Ms120 known issues

  • MS-2938: Switches may fail to provide PoE power to legacy access points (always present)

  • MS-2728: Cable tests may report incorrect cable lengths

Ms130 known issues

  • MS-38070: MS130X mGig ports may fail to establish a link when both sides are forced to 100 Mbps full-duplex. If either side of the connection uses auto-negotiation the link will be established normally

Ms150 known issues

  • MS-38370: MS150 switches may intermittently negotiate USB-C Ethernet adapters at 10 Mbps half-duplex instead of the expected speed for the switchport, requiring a physical reseat to correct the issue.

Ms350x known issues

  • HWMS-375: Switches may experience an unexpected reboot (present since MS 15)

Ms355 known issues

  • HWMS-378: Switches in stacked configurations may experience some ports failing to reconnect after a firmware upgrade.
